text.p: - The emergency committee on gathering taxes may threaten major coal producer with bankruptcy for non-payment of tax.

- Paper, continuing campaign asserting new deputy secretary of Kremlin Security Council Boris Berezovsky has Israeli citizenship, asks who got President Boris Yeltsin to appoint him. Berezovsky denies he has Israeli citizenship.
- Finance Minister Alexander Livshits, a professional economist, has met strong resistance from ministry civil servants during his first 100 days in office.
- The government is borrowing a further $1 billion, after official annoncement of Russia launching Eurobond.

- Russian "paratroops" trying to make Belarus leaders see sense, says the paper in reference to Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin's trip to Minsk late on Thursday for last ditch attempt to calm passions over constitutional referendum.
- The government has failed to improve Russia's economic situation after its first 100 days in office.
- Real names of foreign intelligence agents, working for Moscow, are known only to a very limited number of officials, says a senior official of Russia's intelligence service.
- U.S. plans to spend $240 million to improve security systems at embassy in Moscow.
